messages:
alex_g: Customer (org: BrightLedger) reporting ~15% of inference requests hitting 502s since 03:00 UTC, started after their infra team rotated their outbound NAT/bastion. They see TLS handshake timeouts from our gateway. Verbose curl attached.

mike_r: Can you drop the curl + response headers and the customer IP block? Also region and model id.

alex_g: region: eu-west-1, model: redwood-2.1-large, customer src IP: 52.148.**.0/24, sample curl:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer
```
Response:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.203.45.101) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Failed to receive handshake
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
HTTP/2 stream 1 was reset: INTERNAL_ERROR
curl: (56) Received HTTP/2 stream error
```

sarah_t: Got it. Do we have edge logs for that customer during the window? Any resolver SERVFAILs from their egress path? Customer mentioned they switched to a private NAT with DNS forwarding.

infra-bot: deploy/edge-2026.03.17-11:23:00 completed on eu-west-1 nodes: edge-5a, edge-5b

mike_r: I'll pull the edge proxy traces for that IP block. alex, can you ask the customer to run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -msg` from a host behind their new NAT and paste the handshake debug? We want to see whether SNI reaches us and whether the TLS client sends TLS1.3 ClientHello fully.

alex_g: Customer paste:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.3 Handshake, ClientHello
    <ClientHello truncated in trace - sends 512 bytes then connection reset>
read:errno=104
```
Customer also ran `dig +edns=0 api.redwood.ai` and got truncated responses (TC=1) from their resolver.

jess: Truncated UDP responses -> client falling back to TCP for DNS, increases connection setup time. If their NAT has ephemeral port exhaustion or incorrectly maps TCP DNS queries, that could break name resolution and cause handshake timeouts when the client cannot complete CA bundle fetch/OCSP or even connect to correct IPs.

support-ops: We also see a small spike of 502s (0.8% -> 5%) for eu-west between 03:02-03:20 UTC in our per-customer metrics, matching customer's reported window. Correlating with edge deploy timestamp (infra-bot) — but deploys were on our side earlier and healthy.

mike_r: Edge trace for 18.203.45.101 -> we have many SYN, SYN-ACK, but TLS ClientHello bytes are truncated mid-record on ~20% of flows. The TCP connection doesn't complete application data. This looks like midstream reset from their egress path. No evidence of our cert rotation events in that timeframe.

sarah_t: Noted. Two hypotheses:
- Their DNS responses are being truncated and their resolver does bad TCP fallback causing handshake delays/timeouts.
- Their new NAT/bastion is RST-ing long-lived handshake packets or has port exhaustion.

alex_g: Customer confirmed the bastion performs TCP seq rewriting for port-mapped egress. They will try bypassing the bastion for a few hosts to test.

(10m later)

alex_g: Customer bypassed bastion for 10 hosts -> errors dropped to baseline. They re-routed DNS to 1.1.1.1 and also errors dropped. So root cause likely on their egress: EDNS0 truncation + NAT TCP mapping causing broken DNS/TCP fallback and intermittent connection resets leading to TLS handshake failures.

mike_r: Action items:
- support-ops: mark incident as customer-side networking; include diagnostics we gathered (edge traces, truncated ClientHello counts). (assigned -> support-ops)
- alex_g: Send customer recommended mitigations: switch to non-truncating resolver (Cloudflare/Google), remove TCP rewriting on NAT for port ranges touching ephemeral ports, increase NAT port pool, or enable DNS over TLS/HTTPS as a workaround.
- infra: none required on Redwood side, but note in follow-up that if customer cannot change egress we can recommend routing policies or increasing client-side connect timeouts for that customer temporarily.

jess: Also recommend customer verify they are not doing deep packet inspection that drops TLS handshake fragments. If they insist on the bastion, ensure it preserves full TCP sequence and allows long-lived handshake flows.

alex_g: I'll send TL;DR to customer with packet captures, edge trace ids, and suggested fixes. Closing thread once they confirm mitigation.

support-ops: Documented under support ticket #BL-9437 and attached our edge trace logs. :white_check_mark:

sarah_t: Note for postmortem: these customer-side NAT/DNS path issues keep surfacing — consider an internal doc with a checklist of quick mitigations to send customers (EDNS0 check, `dig +dnssec +edns=1`, `openssl s_client -msg`, try 1.1.1.1). Will draft.

alex_g: Thanks team. Customer will confirm today. :thumbsup:
